proposals: The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should publish state-wise PCPIR investment and employment figures restated to the same date as each national total it reports, so that the roughly 42 per cent of the ₹3,49,192 crore that cannot currently be placed in Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh or Odisha is accounted for.

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should split reported PCPIR investment into amounts actually invested and amounts merely committed, and add commissioned capacity in tonnes by product, so that progress against the ₹7.63 lakh crore projection can be read in output, not only rupees.

The Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals should publish annual domestic production and apparent consumption for each major petrochemical and polymer, mapped to its HSN-8 import codes, so that import-dependency ratios can be computed from official data rather than from industry estimates that, as this post's own audit found, can rest on the wrong codes.

The Directorate General of Trade Remedies should maintain a public tracker of every anti-dumping investigation on chemicals, giving HSN code, initiation date, statutory decision deadline and outcome, so that the status of cases such as those cited here for terephthalic acid and dyes can be confirmed from one primary source.
